properties.name: ROOT CAUSE, THE CLASS (walked, measured): "omitted fields keep their stored value" is ONE sentence copied into 18+ tool descriptions and carried by TWO shared mechanisms (RequiredFields for required fields, upsert_node for untouched properties). Anything a handler DERIVES from the call — a default, a guard, a reply note — or a core constructor that REPLACES bypasses both, and no test enumerates the tools that carry the sentence. Swept on 0.72.0: 4 of 22 revise-capable constructors break the contract, by 4 different mechanisms
properties.statement:
STEP ⑥ OF THE ROOT-CAUSE SKILL for three dev_storyflow reports of one contract failing in three tools (art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27: 09-23 and 09-25 add_change_event `undated`; 09-25 record_finding fact_type; 09-27 add_verification findings), plus the hub's own plan_epoch and external_dependency observations. Walked 2026-09-28.

THE CONTRACT: chg:required-to-create-optional-to-revise (#302, cf3ae62, 2026-08-22) put "CONTENT FIELDS ARE REQUIRED TO CREATE AND OPTIONAL TO REVISE … omitted fields keep their stored value" into every constructor's description. chg:bl183-constructors-merge had earlier made the core add_* helpers merge (upsert_node). ver:constructors-preserve is the class guard.

HOW IT IS IMPLEMENTED (read in source, v0.72.0 = HEAD for these paths):
• RequiredFields (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/service.rs) resolves REQUIRED string/int fields from the stored node, then is consumed by `finish()`. The stored node it fetched (`existing`) is private and is dropped, so nothing else in the handler can read it.
• DesignGraph::upsert_node (reflow2-core graph.rs) merges: supplied keys overwrite, unnamed keys survive.
• EVERYTHING ELSE IS PER HANDLER. A handler that computes from `req` sees the call, not the node after the merge.

THE SWEEP (reflow2-mcp 0.72.0, scratch store; every tool that calls RequiredFields = 22 constructors; create with every declared optional at a non-default value, revise with id + one field, diff get_node before and after, and compare reply keys between create and revise):
• 20 of 22 kept every other stored property.
• plan_epoch: description AND checksum cleared. Core plan_epoch writes with create_node (REPLACE) and carries only `status` forward by hand (the 2026-09-11 instance fix); add_epoch, which uses upsert_node, kept both. The loss of `checksum` is new beyond fact:revising-an-epoch-without-its-description-clears-the-description-2026-09-27.
• record_finding: fact_type defect→finding AND basis forecast→measured. The handler writes `unwrap_or` defaults into the merge bag (#447, 2026-09-07). See fact:root-cause-record-finding-writes-its-defaults-on-every-revise-2026-09-28.
• add_change_event: the only revise-only reply key in the sweep is `undated`, a false note from `req.detected_at.is_none()` (#472, 2026-09-10). See fact:root-cause-the-undated-note-reads-the-call-not-the-stored-node-2026-09-28.
• add_verification: a findings-only revise is REFUSED by a guard on `req.status` (#440, 2026-09-06), measured separately. See fact:root-cause-add-verification-guard-reads-the-call-not-the-stored-run-2026-09-28.
• Outside the 22, external_dependency: re-declaring without `note` dropped the Resource's description on 0.72.0 (core declare_external_dependency uses create_node). Still reproduces fact:re-declaring-a-dependency-drops-the-resources-description-2026-09-23. (Its description does not claim the revise contract, so this is the same mechanism without the same promise.)

FOUR MECHANISMS, ONE CLASS: (1) a handler DEFAULT written into the merge (record_finding); (2) a handler NOTE computed from the call (add_change_event); (3) a handler GUARD computed from the call (add_verification); (4) a core constructor that REPLACES and carries fields forward by hand (plan_epoch, external_dependency). The shared mechanisms are correct wherever they are used; each instance is code that goes around them.

CANDIDATES FOR THE CLASS CAUSE, and what refuted them: (a) the shared merge is broken — refuted, 20/22 keep everything and upsert_node is correct. (b) One bad commit — refuted, the instances come from #440, #447 and #472 on three different days plus a July core constructor. (c) The contract is enforced by a mechanism some tools bypass, and nothing checks the whole set — HOLDS. Every field-reported instance was added AFTER #302 stated the contract, in code written for the create case; RequiredFields offers no merged view to the rest of the handler; and the tests enumerate INSTANCES. constructors_preserve.rs covers the core of 6 types, last run 2026-08-02. required_to_create_optional_to_revise.rs spot-checks Requirement, Verification and DesignEpoch (add_epoch, not plan_epoch). an_undated_change_event_says_so.rs covers the create path only. None covers a revise of record_finding, add_change_event, add_verification or plan_epoch. (d) The observations are wrong — refuted, all four reproduce on a clean store.

WOULD THE FIX STOP THE OTHER OCCURRENCES? A fix to any one instance would not: 09-23/09-25 (note), 09-25 (default) and 09-27 (guard) are three different lines of code. That is why this is the cause and each instance only a trigger. The same shape has been recorded before: #440's rationale ("a fix placed in one handler recurred on its sibling within a day"), fact:the-parallel-batch-class-recurred-because-only-its-instance-was-fixed, and the plan_epoch STATUS reset (fixed 09-11 for one field; the description loss is the same write, still open).

WHAT A CLASS-PINNING TEST WOULD ASSERT (not written; out of scope): a table-driven test over EVERY tool whose description contains "OPTIONAL TO REVISE", enumerated from the served tool list rather than hand-listed, so a new or changed tool joins automatically. For each: create with every declared optional property at a non-default value; revise with id + one field; assert (i) every other stored property is byte-identical, and (ii) the revise reply carries no note, and the call no refusal, about a field the merged node holds. Today it would fail on plan_epoch, record_finding, add_change_event and add_verification. Counterweights: a first create still lands the documented defaults; an explicitly passed value still overwrites.

SHAPE OF THE CLASS FIX (for whoever builds it; not decided): give handlers the merged node. For example, RequiredFields keeps and exposes `existing`, and defaults, guards and notes read "passed, else stored, else default". Also route plan_epoch and declare_external_dependency through upsert_node. The open design question — whether a guard that exists to force a restatement should read the merged node — is brainstormed in dec:idea-revise-notes-guards-and-defaults-read-the-merged-node.

NOT ESTABLISHED: edges and list-valued fields (affected, verifies, related_to, steps) were not swept; one value per property, not combinations; setters (set_*) and link_artifact not swept; current source read and diffed against v0.72.0, not built.

PARTLY FIXED 2026-09-29; left open on purpose. Fixed by reflow2 PR #624 (squash 8588b7a). Its change record, chg:a-revise-keeps-what-it-was-not-passed, INVALIDATES this fact in the committed design; it is not in this live store. What moved:
- mechanism (1), the record_finding default;
- mechanism (2), the add_change_event note, now read from the merged node;
- mechanism (4), plan_epoch;
- the "guarded by instances" half: a_revise_keeps_what_it_was_not_passed.rs reads its list from the served tool list, so every tool promising "optional to revise" is covered automatically;
- also, seven tools that stored name "" on an id-only create.
What still holds:
- mechanism (3): add_verification still refuses a findings-only revise. Its refusal now names the stored verdict, but whether it may inherit it is open in dec:idea-revise-notes-guards-and-defaults-read-the-merged-node;
- external_dependency still replaces on re-declare, deliberately unchanged because it does not promise "optional to revise".
